Molecular mechanisms driving DNPC pathogenesis and therapeutic resistance

Molecular mechanisms driving DNPC pathogenesis and therapeutic resistance. a Epigenetic and transcriptional regulation drives lineage plasticity. On the one hand, ADT induces or occurs concurrently with KMT2C mutation/loss which activates TET enzymes, leading to PROX1 promoter demethylation and consequent PROX1 overexpression. PROX1 interacts with HDAC complexes, suppressing apoptosis and enhancing cell survival. Concurrently, ADT combined with KMT2C mutation/loss decreases ASPP2 levels, resulting in increased SREBP1c and Delta Np63 expression. Delta Np63 drives FASN activity and facilitates HRAS palmitoylation, leading to constitutive activation of MAPK signaling, thereby enabling DNPC transdifferentiation and ADT resistance. On the other hand, Pathologically activated PRC1 complex induces CCL2 expression. CCL2 binding to CCR2 and CCR4 receptors promotes infiltration of TAMs and MDSCs, establishing an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment that enhances cancer stemness and self-renewal, facilitating metastasis. Concurrent DKK1 promoter demethylation contributes to NK cell functional inactivation. b Aberrant activation of compensatory signaling pathways in DNPC. Following ADT pressure, FGF ligands activate FGFR receptors, triggering a phosphorylation cascade involving RAF, MEK, and ERK. This signaling axis converges with parallel pathways: JNK-mediated phosphorylation and activation of STAT transcription factors, alongside UCH-L1-dependent stabilization of mTORC1 signaling. Upregulated regulators amplify oncogenic signaling while suppressing androgen-responsive genes. This signaling landscape culminates in increased activity of MYC oncogenic targets, CDK4/6-RB-E2F mediated cell cycle progression, and Bcl-2 dependent suppression of apoptosis, collectively driving DNPC cell survival and proliferation independently of androgen receptor signaling. DNPC double-negative prostate cancer, ADT androgen deprivation therapy, TAMs Tumor-Associated Macrophages, MDSCs Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells
